name: search_workspace
description: Search file contents across the workspace by pattern. The tool for finding where something is defined, referenced, or mentioned without reading every candidate file by hand.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for, matched against file content.

path.description: Directory to scope the search to, relative to the workspace root. Defaults to the whole workspace.

glob.description: Optional filename filter, e.g. "*.ts" or "**/*.md". Narrows which files are searched before the pattern is applied.

max_results.description: Upper bound on matches returned. A search that would exceed this is truncated and `truncated` is set.

file.description: Workspace-relative path of the matching file.

text.description: The matching line's content, for context. Not the whole file.

truncated.description: True if `max_results` cut the match list short of every occurrence in the workspace.

files_searched.description: Number of files the search actually scanned, for judging how broad the sweep was.

errors.description: `pattern` is not a valid regular expression.
The `path` scope does not exist in the workspace.
`path` resolves outside the workspace root and was refused before any search was attempted.

safety_notes: Read-only, and bounded by construction: `max_results` and `files_searched` exist so a caller never has to guess whether a search was exhaustive or quietly partial. Binary files are skipped rather than scanned byte-for-byte against a text pattern, and skipped files are not counted as searched. A search returning zero matches is a real, reportable result — 'not found by this search' — and must not be presented as 'does not exist anywhere in the workspace,' which is a stronger claim this tool cannot support on its own.
